Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

intellectual adjective

of the mind

also intellectual work, intellectual pursuits, intellectual life

classical

Cic. Sen. 38: eās rēs tueor animī nōn corporis vīribus (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Off. 1.123: exercitātiōnēs animī

animī

genitive of animus, after the noun

of the mind (as against the body)

Latin says “of the mind” with the genitive, usually set against corporis (see mind).

Other words

  • studia, studiōrum n. pl. — intellectual pursuits, studies

    noun, second declension, plural · also used · classical · Cic. Rosc. Am. 46: studia doctrīnae (Lewis & Short)

    The plural of studium, eagerness; with a genitive, the pursuit itself: studia doctrīnae, litterārum.

  • intellēctuālis, intellēctuāle — relating to the understanding

    adjective, third declension · also used · late Latin · Apul. Dogm. Plat. 1.3; Aug. Gen. ad Lit. 12.7 (Lewis & Short)

    A word of late philosophy, from intellēctus, understanding; the long ē by Lachmann’s law, as in lēctus.

Examples

  • senibus autem labōrēs corporis minuendī, exercitātiōnēs animī etiam augendae videntur

    for the old, bodily labour should be lessened, and exercise of the mind even increasedCic. Off. 1.123

  • eās rēs tueor animī nōn corporis vīribus

    I keep up these things with the strength of my mind, not of my bodyCic. Sen. 38 (Lewis & Short)

See also intellectual, mind, intelligence.

SourcesLewis & Short: animus · Lewis & Short: studium · Lewis & Short: intellectualis

Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cicero-philosophica), checked against the editions named there.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
